mechanism: Full-covariance CMA-ES with restart regimes using small and large populations.
recommendation: Shares the CMA-ES core; consider replacing the base variant when studying restarts or larger budgets.
reference_status: Shares the ModCMA framework references; a BIPOP restart reference is supplied separately.
reference: Hansen (2009), Benchmarking a BI-Population CMA-ES on the BBOB-2009 Function Testbed; Framework references are the same as for modcma_base.

mechanism: Samples a multivariate Gaussian and adapts its mean, full covariance matrix, and step size to learn variable dependencies.
recommendation: Selected: represents search-distribution adaptation and learning of variable interactions.
reference_status: Package METADATA/README explicitly cites the modular framework papers; CMA theory references are supplied separately.
reference: van Rijn et al. (2016), Evolving the Structure of Evolution Strategies; de Nobel et al. (2021), Tuning as a Means of Assessing the Benefits of New Ideas in Interplay with Existing Algorithmic Modules. Theory: Hansen and Ostermeier (2001), Completely Derandomized Self-Adaptation in Evolution Strategies; Hansen (2016), The CMA Evolution Strategy: A Tutorial.

mechanism: Combines current-to-pbest differential mutation, an external archive, success-history adaptation of F/CR, and population reduction based on consumed evaluations.
recommendation: Selected: represents adaptive DE; report it as this benchmark's modular L-SHADE configuration.
reference_status: Package README explicitly provides an L-SHADE configuration; the corresponding paper is supplied separately. Current parameters differ from the paper.
reference: Tanabe and Fukunaga (2014), Improving the Search Performance of SHADE Using Linear Population Size Reduction.

mechanism: Fixed-parameter DE/rand/1/bin uses random population members and difference vectors, followed by crossover and greedy selection.
recommendation: Selected: provides a basic-DE comparison against adaptive DE.
reference_status: Package README describes modular DE; no dedicated paper for this configuration was found. The reference supplies family-level background.
reference: Storn and Price (1997), Differential Evolution – A Simple and Efficient Heuristic for Global Optimization over Continuous Spaces.

mechanism: Calls SciPy BFGS, estimates gradients by finite differences, and uses quasi-Newton updates; the underlying wrapper allows random restarts.
recommendation: Selected: represents local slope and curvature information; this configuration creates one BFGS instance.
reference_status: No dedicated MultiBFGS paper citation was found. The local call chain confirms BFGS; the theoretical reference is supplementary.
reference: Fletcher (1970), A new approach to variable metric algorithms. BFGS was independently developed by several authors; this is one foundational reference. See SciPy BFGS documentation for implementation details.

mechanism: Performs one-dimensional searches along a set of directions and updates that set without constructing numerical gradients.
recommendation: Selected: represents derivative-free direction-set local search.
reference_status: No dedicated paper citation for the Nevergrad Powell wrapper was found; the theoretical reference is supplementary.
reference: Powell (1964), An efficient method for finding the minimum of a function of several variables without calculating derivatives. The implementation calls SciPy modified Powell.

mechanism: Uses a diagonal covariance configuration of CMA to learn coordinate scales without full cross-variable correlations.
recommendation: Prioritize for a separability study; it is a structurally distinct variant within the CMA family.
reference_status: Constructed with diagonal=True in the library; the reference provides background on diagonal/separable CMA.
reference: Ros and Hansen (2008), A Simple Modification in CMA-ES Achieving Linear Time and Space Complexity.

mechanism: Generates one Gaussian-mutated offspring from one parent, retains the better solution, and adapts the global step size using success information.
recommendation: Selected: a simple stochastic local-search baseline without covariance learning.
reference_status: Parameter documentation discusses Gaussian mutation and success-based step-size rules; there is no unique dedicated paper for this default wrapper.
reference: Beyer and Schwefel (2002), Evolution strategies – A comprehensive introduction. This is a family-level review, not a dedicated paper for the default Nevergrad implementation.

mechanism: The inspected Nevergrad implementation forms a donor from the current individual, a random difference vector, and a direction toward the best solution, then applies crossover.
recommendation: Overlaps with the DE family; its name does not imply DE/rand/1.
reference_status: The class documentation describes DE settings. The basic-DE reference is supplementary, not an equation-level specification of this configuration.
reference: Storn and Price (1997), Differential Evolution – A Simple and Efficient Heuristic for Global Optimization over Continuous Spaces.

mechanism: Uses heavy-tailed Levy steps to generate candidates, together with nest replacement and local differential perturbations.
recommendation: Not selected in the final compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: X.-S. Yang and D. Suash. Cuckoo search via Lévy flights. World Congress on Nature & Biologically Inspired Computing (2009).

mechanism: Uses differential mutation from random individuals, crossover, and greedy replacement.
recommendation: Overlaps with basic ModDE; retaining both adds limited mechanism coverage to a compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: R. Storn. On the usage of differential evolution for function optimization. Proceedings of North American Fuzzy Information Processing (1996).

mechanism: Uses evaporation-inspired phase scheduling, fitness-dependent evaporation masks, and population difference vectors.
recommendation: Combines differential updates and scheduling, overlapping with the selected DE and EO mechanisms.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: A. Kaveh and T. Bakhshpoori. Water Evaporation Optimization: A novel physically inspired optimization algorithm. Computers & Structures (2016).

mechanism: Allocates queues around leading solutions and applies staged Gamma-distributed perturbations and population differences.
recommendation: A candidate for grouped, multistage search; lower priority than the core mechanisms in this compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: J. Zhang et al. Queuing search algorithm: A novel metaheuristic algorithm for solving engineering optimization problems. Applied Mathematical Modelling (2018).

mechanism: Uses the best pack member and coordinate-wise pack medians for updates, with migration between packs.
recommendation: Represents subpopulations and population statistics; not selected in the final compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: J. Pierezan and L. Coelho. Coyote Optimization Algorithm: A New Metaheuristic for Global Optimization Problems. IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (2018).

mechanism: Uses mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism phases involving pairwise interactions and partial replacement.
recommendation: An optional twelfth algorithm to add explicit symbiotic pairwise interactions.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: M.-Y. Cheng and D. Prayogo. Symbiotic Organisms Search: A new metaheuristic optimization algorithm. Computers & Structures (2014).

mechanism: Combines production, consumption, and decomposition phases using bounded random sampling, population differences, and perturbations around the best solution.
recommendation: A multistage hybrid with operators overlapping those already selected.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: W. Zhao, L. Wang and Z. Zhang. Artificial ecosystem-based optimization: a novel nature-inspired meta-heuristic algorithm. Neural Computing and Applications (2019).

mechanism: Separates sunspot and canopy individuals by fitness and uses neighbor-difference flight moves and fallback updates.
recommendation: Artificial Butterfly Optimization, distinct from BOA; overlaps with role-based and differential search.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: X. Qi, Y. Zhu and H. Zhang. A new meta-heuristic butterfly-inspired algorithm. Journal of Computational Science (2017).

mechanism: Uses survival counters to bias selection and generates candidates through three-parent differential mutation and crossover.
recommendation: Despite its immune-system terminology, its main candidate-generation operator resembles DE.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: C. Villaseñor et al. Germinal center optimization algorithm. International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems (2018).

mechanism: Combines lightning-inspired directions, exponential/Gaussian random steps, and an energy-decay schedule.
recommendation: Overlaps with multiscale random search and time-dependent scheduling.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: H. Shareef, A. Ibrahim and A. Mutlag. Lightning search algorithm. Applied Soft Computing (2015).

mechanism: Combines large runner perturbations, small root searches, stagnation detection, and restarts.
recommendation: Provides multiscale local/global search; omitted to keep the set compact, with CS covering long jumps.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: F. Merrikh-Bayat. The runner-root algorithm: A metaheuristic for solving unimodal and multimodal optimization problems inspired by runners and roots of plants in nature. Applied Soft Computing (2015).

mechanism: Maintains velocity and personal-best memory and combines global-best guidance with differences between historical positions.
recommendation: Selected: represents velocity-based search with memory; it is a PSO variant, not the complete constrained framework of its source paper.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: H. Lu and W. Chen. Self-adaptive velocity particle swarm optimization for solving constrained optimization problems. Journal of global optimization (2008).

mechanism: Allocates offspring counts by fitness, reproduces through Gaussian dispersal with decreasing variance, and truncates the population competitively.
recommendation: Represents reproduction and variance scheduling; its botanical metaphor alone does not establish a separate search paradigm.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: A. R. Mehrabian and C. Lucas. A novel numerical optimization algorithm inspired from weed colonization. Ecological informatics (2006).

mechanism: Maintains four elite solutions and their mean as an equilibrium pool and updates positions using time-dependent exponential and generation terms.
recommendation: Not selected in the final compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: A. Faramarzi et al. Equilibrium optimizer: A novel optimization algorithm. Knowledge-Based Systems (2020).

mechanism: Moves a leader around the best solution while followers update through chain-like averaging.
recommendation: Salp Swarm Algorithm, not Sparrow Search Algorithm.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: S. Mirjalili et al. Salp Swarm Algorithm: A bio-inspired optimizer for engineering design problems. Advances in Engineering Software (2017).

mechanism: Stores and shuffles a historical population, mutates using historical-current differences, and applies crossover and greedy selection.
recommendation: Backtracking Search, not Bird Swarm; an option for expanding the differential-search family.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: P. Civicioglu. Backtracking search optimization algorithm for numerical optimization problems. Applied Mathematics and Computation (2013).

mechanism: Uses employed-bee search, onlooker allocation of search effort, and scout handling of stagnating locations.
recommendation: Not selected in the final compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: D. Karaboga and B. Basturk. A powerful and efficient algorithm for numerical function optimization: Artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm. Journal of Global Optimization (2007).

mechanism: Computes distance-dependent attraction/repulsion, contracts the interaction scale, and uses best-solution guidance.
recommendation: Distinct from PSO's personal-best velocity mechanism; can replace EO to emphasize spatial pairwise interactions.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: S. Saremi, S. Mirjalili and A. Lewis. Grasshopper Optimisation Algorithm: Theory and application. Advances in Engineering Software (2017).

mechanism: Combines fitness-based selection, real-valued arithmetic crossover, Gaussian mutation, and survivor selection from parents and offspring.
recommendation: Selected: represents recombination-centered evolutionary search; this is a real-coded GA.
reference_status: The class docstring cites Mitchell's GA textbook (1998 in the library), not a dedicated implementation paper; the publisher link describes the 1996 edition.
reference: M. Mitchell. An introduction to genetic algorithms. MIT Press (1998).

mechanism: Converts fitness into weights and updates solutions using pulls from stronger individuals, displacement, and noise.
recommendation: Shares its theoretical family with mealpy_OriginalTWO; avoid counting both as independent mechanisms.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: A. Kaveh. Tug of War Optimization. Advances in Metaheuristic Algorithms for Optimal Design of Structures (2016).

mechanism: Adds relativistic velocity handling to PSO updates.
recommendation: Another PSO variant alongside SAVPSO; RPSO here means Relativistic PSO.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: M. Roder, G. H. de Rosa, L. A. Passos, A. L. D. Rossi and J. P. Papa. Harnessing Particle Swarm Optimization Through Relativistic Velocity. IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (2020).

mechanism: Combines relocation toward the best solution, local noticing moves, and updates of weak individuals near an elite habitat.
recommendation: A composite position-perturbation method; the compact set prioritizes more directly interpretable mechanisms.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: D. Polap and M. Woźniak. Red fox optimization algorithm. Expert Systems with Applications (2021).

mechanism: Derives masses from fitness, computes acceleration from atomic potentials and best-solution constraints, and updates velocity and position.
recommendation: Has velocity state but potential-field driving forces; can replace EO when emphasizing force-based models.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: W. Zhao, L. Wang and Z. Zhang. A novel atom search optimization for dispersion coefficient estimation in groundwater. Future Generation Computer Systems (2019).

mechanism: Switches probabilistically between multiplication/division and addition/subtraction around the best solution according to time.
recommendation: Arithmetic Optimization, not Aquila; distinct arithmetic operators do not automatically require a slot in the compact set.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: L. Abualigah et al. The Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm. Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering (2021).

mechanism: Uses within-team best solutions, the global best, and inter-team competition to guide updates.
recommendation: Most Valuable Player Algorithm; belongs to grouped cooperation and competition.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: H. Bouchekara. Most Valuable Player Algorithm: a novel optimization algorithm inspired from sport. Operational Research (2017).

mechanism: Combines current-to-pbest mutation, an external archive, and successful-sample updates of the F/CR distribution means.
recommendation: A clear adaptive-DE alternative if a modular L-SHADE configuration is undesirable.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: [1] Zhang, J. and Sanderson, A.C., 2009. JADE: adaptive differential evolution with optional external archive. IEEE Transactions on evolutionary computation, 13(5), pp.945-958.

mechanism: Learns selection probabilities for two DE mutation strategies and adapts crossover parameters.
recommendation: The Qin-Suganthan SaDE variant, not a generic label for all self-adaptive DE or jDE.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: [1] Qin, A.K. and Suganthan, P.N., 2005, September. Self-adaptive differential evolution algorithm for numerical optimization. In 2005 IEEE congress on evolutionary computation (Vol. 2, pp. 1785-1791). IEEE.

mechanism: Declares success-history adaptation and linear population reduction, but the inspected 2.5.3 code still generates offspring using fixed pop_size.
recommendation: Not the preferred L-SHADE representative: the inspected implementation differs from the paper's actual population reduction.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: [1] Tanabe, R. and Fukunaga, A.S., 2014, July. Improving the search performance of SHADE using linear population size reduction. In 2014 IEEE congress on evolutionary computation (CEC) (pp. 1658-1665). IEEE.

mechanism: Stores search clues, uses social and individual differential-search phases, and resets after stagnation.
recommendation: Adds cooperative search with memory; omitted from the compact selection.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: [1] Shabani, A., Asgarian, B., Gharebaghi, S.A., Salido, M.A. and Giret, A., 2019. A new optimization algorithm based on search and rescue operations. Mathematical Problems in Engineering, 2019.

mechanism: Uses fitness-based weights, team pulling forces, random displacement, and boundary handling.
recommendation: Same theoretical family as opy_TWO; implementations across libraries are not independent principles.
reference_status: The class docstring explicitly provides a reference or a source-paper link.
reference: [1] Kaveh, A., 2017. Tug of war optimization. In Advances in metaheuristic algorithms for optimal design of structures (pp. 451-487). Springer, Cham.

mechanism: Generates Gaussian ES offspring and additional Levy offspring, then truncates their union with the parents.
recommendation: A library-developed hybrid; the general ES reference is not a dedicated paper for this variant.
reference_status: The class docstring provides a reference or link and explicitly identifies a developed version; this does not establish a dedicated paper for the variant.
reference: [1] Beyer, H.G. and Schwefel, H.P., 2002. Evolution strategies–a comprehensive introduction. Natural computing, 1(1), pp.3-52.

mechanism: Combines virus diffusion, Gaussian infection around an elite mean, and differential immune-response updates.
recommendation: A library-developed version, not a direct equation-by-equation reproduction of original Virus Colony Search.
reference_status: The class docstring provides a reference or link and explicitly identifies a developed version; this does not establish a dedicated paper for the variant.
reference: Li, Zhao, Weng and Han (2016), A novel nature-inspired algorithm for optimization: Virus colony search. The class documentation directly supplies the DOI.
